title: Senior Iranian official vows to hit cables, data centers, and AI facilities if war escalates again
source_used: Fortune (Middle East roundup of 11 Oct 2026); fulltext fetched by the main session. The identical text was also read on PBS News (pbs.org/newshour/world/iran-calls-latest-u-s-proposal-to-end-war-insufficient-as-netanyahus-corruption-trial-resumes, byline Michael D. Regan, PBS NewsHour senior digital editor, page dated 11 Oct 2026 5:43 PM EDT) to check the chain of credit; WANA (Iranian agency, datelined Oct 11) was read to date the remarks.
key_facts: The roundup says the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, Mohsen Rezaei (a former Revolutionary Guard commander), told Iran's state-run IRNA news agency that Tehran finds the latest US response to a proposal to end the war 'insufficient'.
Rezaei threatened 'cables, data centers, AI facilities and other sites in the region' if intense fighting breaks out again; no specific site, country or company is named.

He added that Iran is no longer responding to the US and that Washington must clarify certain issues, without details; he said the US has accepted some of Iran's seven conditions but others remain unclear.

Efforts at negotiations to end the war and fully open the Strait of Hormuz 'limp along'; a sped-up agreement proposed by Iran's delegation at last month's UN gathering was rejected, but the two sides remain in contact through mediation.
The earlier memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran collapsed days after it was signed in June.

The Revolutionary Guard's navy warned that any ship in the strait that turns off its navigation and identification systems would be 'identified as hostile', according to IRNA; attacks on ships in the strait have increased since Iran's proposal was rejected, and one attack was reported on Sunday.
The roundup also covers other Middle East news (Netanyahu's corruption trial, attacks on Riyadh airport, Gaza and Lebanon), which is not part of this item.
quote_evidence: Rezaei also threatened "cables, data centers, AI facilities and other sites in the region" if intense fighting breaks out again.
The comments by Mohsen Rezaei, a former Revolutionary Guard commander, were carried by Iran's state-run IRNA news agency.
Attacks on ships transiting the strait have increased since Iran's proposal was rejected.
why_it_matters_hint: A conditional Iranian threat names data centers, cables and AI facilities in the region as possible targets if the US-Iran war escalates, while talks to end it stall.
event_date: Reported 11 Oct 2026 (PBS page 11 Oct 5:43 PM EDT; WANA datelined Oct 11); the roundup is headed 'latest news ... on Saturday' but also covers Sunday, and the exact time of Rezaei's remarks is not stated.
notes: The Fortune page and the PBS News page carry identical text; PBS shows the byline of its senior digital editor Michael D. Regan, Fortune's copy as fetched shows no byline or credit, and the publication order could not be settled, so the source line names Fortune with the PBS copy and IRNA, which carried Rezaei's words (WANA, an Iranian outlet, corroborates them). The article calls him head of the Supreme National Security Council; WANA calls him its Secretary. The pool score of 6 is kept because outside reporting dates the remarks to 11 Oct. No undersea cables are mentioned in this text, only 'cables'. No company or site is named.
